patch_description: Key insight from the metrics: the benchmark score favors configurations where the convex hull itself is a fixed, maximal-area shape. Instead of scattering points in a unit square (where the hull area shrinks and many near-collinear boundary triples appear), we anchor three points at the vertices of a unit-area equilateral triangle, so the hull area is exactly 1 and min_area_normalized equals the raw minimum triangle area. The remaining 10 points are optimized with a deterministic, seeded annealing/perturbation scheme exploiting 3-fold symmetry in the initialization. All 286 triangle areas are computed with precomputed triple indices in a single vectorized NumPy operation. Points are handled in barycentric coordinates w.r.t. the triangle and projected (clipped to nonnegative, renormalized) so they always stay inside the convex region. An adaptive step-size random-perturbation refinement with a lexicographic tie-break (larger minimum area wins) drives the minimum triangle area up, targeting a normalized value near or above the benchmark constant 0.0309.
